Definition: from G1909 and G2749; to rest upon (literally or figuratively):--impose, be instant, (be) laid (there-, up-)on, (when) lay (on), lie (on), press upon.
BiblicalUsage: Epikeimai means to lie upon, to rest upon, to press — a weight that sits on something. The people pressed upon Jesus to hear the word; a stone lay upon the tomb of Lazarus; a tempest lay upon the ship for many days; necessity is laid upon Paul to preach; and divers washings were imposed until the time of reformation.
TheologicalSignificance: The crowd's pressure, the stone's weight, the storm's burden — and the necessity laid on Paul, which he called a woe if he did not preach. I believe what lies upon us shows what carries us, and I want the necessity of the gospel to lie on me the way it lay on him.
RelatedEvents: Raising of Lazarus; Paul Shipwrecked on Malta
